I know this will likely be viewed as fat sympathy and disregarded, but I'd like to weigh in (haha, get it?) on this as a former Thai boxing instructor and personal trainer.

The only time I advocated specific diets, were for my fighters trying to cut weight before a bout, and that was explicitly told them to be temporary. When people asked me which ones were the best, I'd answer honestly that I didn't think they should chase down a specific diet fad. Cutting out all carbs instead of reducing them, or cholestoral, or sugar, or whatever else the demon of the day is is not a good long-term solution to me. Instead, I always, always, always advocated lifestyle changes instead.

I told my students repeatedly: you will only be dumb enough to eat McDonald's before my class one time. I don't have to give you diet advice, because you're going to learn quickly that eating garbage makes you feel like crap. And you will notice a difference in your cardio, energy, and performance based on what you shovel into your mouth before you come. And you're going to find out who was dumb enough to drink the night before, 'cause they're gonna be throwing up in the bathroom and smelling like crap... they would only do that once either.

When pressed, 'what did you eat Khun Khru?' I would answer honestly with what I had had that day. And furthermore, after class was over, I usually took the students over to a healthy restaurant (admittedly, usually a Thai restaurant) and we would eat lunch together. I believe in leading by example, so I would always order something healthy first and the students would wind up following suit.

One of my students lost 50 pounds, and the only changes he made in his life were coming to my class for 2 hours a day on Saturdays. I always told my students that they would despise me, but they would love the way their body would start to look in a relatively short time frame. I was a fan of taking a 'before' picture of the student on the first day, and then having them take their picture again every month so that they could see the results in front of their eyes even if they weren't on a scale every day.

That all being said, fuck this individual. I get the message he's trying to convey, but that method of delivery is more harmful than good. I may not be a fan of diets personally (exercise is FTW!) and I may not advocate them wholesale, but it's dangerous to say ignore them altogether. It's important to discuss things with a nutritionist once in a while. Even better if you have a good PCP that monitors your levels regularly, and a really good one can give you tips on nutrients and diet advice that you need based on your own DNA now.

Got a Haze dripper by Tobeco in the mail yesterday - anyone else gotten a chance to run this thing?

As a single-coil prefered kind of guy, this thing is just tops. I watched a few videos of it on YouTube before and kind of brushed it off initially as a gimmicky, almost niche thing that wants to dip its toes into the Genny realm a bit. Meh. But for under a twenty spot, shipped, I figured it wouldn't be too hard on the wallet to pick one up and play with it. A novelty toy, if anything.

But I really like this thing. It doesn't leak, at all. Not weeping at the seams, not drops coming out of the intake, nothing. I've run half a dozen of the "tanks" through it now and I don't have so much as condensation build-up. I like it. Airflow is more or less designed more for single coils than dual, but getting that wide-open airflow blasting directly onto a contact coil is giving plumes of vapor and delicious, defined flavor. The offset drip tip does its job preventing most spitback, but I'd be a liar if I said I never got any at all. Much less so than a straight dripper, I'll say that.

As with most my drippers, I'm using elfwick - and that, too, hasn't let me down a single time yet. Thirsty, thirsty fibers like feeding that juice to the coil with a nice, clean taste and no added aftertaste. Beautiful set up, the two.

I may not be taking it to work and out and about with me (I don't particularly like taking juice out with me, and prefer to stick to closed-tank systems in that case) - but at home, bumming around and whatnot, this thing is cool, effective, and worth every penny. I'm a fan.

If you're on the fence, do it. It's cheap enough to not break the bank, it's not a "game changer," but it works and it works well. I give it a thumb's up.
